method.exact: Block counts, amp/cab counts, bypassed-alternate counts and slot arithmetic come straight from the recipe data and published device specs.
method.estimated: DSP percentages come from a local per-role weight table (DSP_WEIGHTS in the generator). They only decide the fits/tight boundary — never a 'no' on their own.
method.refused: Kemper verdicts are 'not_applicable': the amp is a user-sourced profile, so a fit verdict would be invented.
method.scope: A verdict answers 'does this chain load on this device', not 'does this device sound like the record'. translation_fidelity flags recipes whose per-platform translation was already a reduction of the Helix chain.

devices.label: Helix Floor / LT / Rack
devices.note: 32 blocks across two DSP paths, 8 per sub-path. Chains over 8 blocks split across path 1 and path 2 — which is exactly what our .hlx exporter already does.

devices.label: HX Stomp
devices.note: 8 blocks, one DSP, three footswitches. The block cap and the DSP ceiling bite at roughly the same time once an amp and a cab are in the chain.

devices.label: HX Stomp XL
devices.note: Identical DSP and block count to the HX Stomp — the XL buys footswitches and a fourth snapshot, not headroom. Its verdicts differ from the Stomp only in the footswitch caveat.

devices.label: POD Go
devices.spec_source: docs/platform-knowledge/line6-helix.md § Product Line (7 blocks, 1 amp, 1 cab)
devices.note: Fixed chain: dedicated Wah, Volume/Pan, Amp, Cab/IR, EQ and FX Loop positions, plus 4 freely assignable blocks. Anything that isn't a wah, volume, amp, cab or EQ has to fit in those 4.

devices.label: Quad Cortex
devices.note: 4 rows x 8 columns = 32 slots. A single series lane is 8 columns wide; longer chains need a second row.

devices.label: Fractal FM3
devices.note: The 4x12 grid is never the limit on an FM3 — CPU is. One amp plus a cab plus a handful of effects is the working envelope, and bypassing a block does not give the CPU back.

devices.label: Fractal FM9
devices.note: Roughly twice the FM3's processing on the same 4x12 grid. Nothing in our library comes close to filling it.

devices.label: Kemper Profiler
devices.note: The amp isn't modelled — it's a profile you source yourself. Our Kemper translations name a Rig Exchange search, not a specific rig, so a fit verdict would be a guess.

devices.label: Katana Gen 3
devices.note: One amp character plus five effect slots — Booster, Mod, FX, Delay, Reverb — each drawing from its own pool. Two overdrives is one overdrive too many.

srv-pride-and-joy-rhythm.title: SRV's Pride and Joy Rhythm Tone

helix_floor_lt.reason: 9 blocks — over the 8-block limit for a single path, so it lands across both DSP paths. Routine on a Helix Floor / LT / Rack: 32 blocks total, est. 45% of available DSP.

hx_stomp.reason: 9 blocks against the HX Stomp's 8. Lose 1 bypassed alternate (Kinky Boost) and you're at 8 of 8, est. 84% DSP. Nothing you actually hear changes — what you give up is the alternate voicings parked in the chain for stomping.

hx_stomp_xl.reason: 9 blocks against the HX Stomp XL's 8. Lose 1 bypassed alternate (Kinky Boost) and you're at 8 of 8, est. 84% DSP. Nothing you actually hear changes — what you give up is the alternate voicings parked in the chain for stomping.

pod_go.reason: 5 blocks want POD Go's four free positions, but 2 of them are bypassed alternates (Kinky Boost and Minotaur). Pick the drive you want, leave the others out, and it fits: Deluxe Comp, Scream 808 and Spring.
caveats: The dual-mic cab collapses to a single mic — POD Go's Cab/IR slot is one cab, one mic. You lose the blend, not the character.

quad_cortex.reason: 6 blocks on a 32-slot grid, est. 29% CPU.

fractal_fm3.reason: 6 blocks on a 48-slot grid, est. 66% CPU.

fractal_fm9.reason: 6 blocks on a 48-slot grid, est. 33% CPU.

kemper.reason: We won't call this one. On a Kemper the amp is a profile you source yourself, and our translation points at a Rig Exchange search rather than a specific rig — so whether this tone "fits" depends on a profile we didn't ship and can't see. What we can say: 2 pre-stack stomps (slots A–D hold four) and 1 post-stack effect (X/MOD/DLY/REV holds four) — the effects side fits an MK1 layout, and an MK2's twenty slots aren't remotely troubled. Worth knowing: our Kemper Profiler translation already leaves out the EQ the Helix chain uses, so this is a capacity verdict on a chain we'd already trimmed.
caveats: Effect-slot arithmetic is computed; the amp match is not.
Slot counts assume an MK1 (4 pre + 4 post). MK2 hardware has 20.

katana_gen3.reason: 2 of the Katana's five effect slots, one per category — the amp character covers the amp and cab, so nothing is competing. Worth knowing: our Katana Gen 3 translation already leaves out the compressor and EQ the Helix chain uses, so this is a capacity verdict on a chain we'd already trimmed. That's deliberate — RECIPE_STANDARD.md exempts Katana Gen 3 from mirroring compressor and EQ because the hardware handles them inside the amp section. It still means this isn't block-for-block the Helix tone.
caveats: The Katana's amp character is a voicing, not a model of the specific amp — the closest character, not a match.
